title: Non-stationary A/B Tests

problem.claim: Nonstationarity, including time-of-day effects, can arise in business metrics and affect A/B tests.

gap.claim: Inadequately addressing nonstationarity can make A/B tests statistically inefficient or invalid and lead to wrong conclusions.

contributions.claim: A framework is developed for modeling and statistically analyzing nonstationary A/B tests.
An estimator treats time as a continuous covariate and performs post-stratification with a sample-dependent number of stratification levels without changing existing A/B test infrastructure.
A time-grouped randomization approach is proposed to improve treatment-control balance when experiment design permits it.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe the framework, estimator, and time-grouped randomization approach as new proposals for nonstationary A/B tests.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors prove a central limit theorem in a natural limiting regime under nonstationarity, enabling valid large-sample statistical inference.
The proposed estimator is shown to attain the minimum asymptotic variance among all estimators.
Numerical experiments are conducted to illustrate the theoretical analysis.

narrative_sequence.summary: A/B tests are widely used by data-driven enterprises for decision-making and testing ideas.
Nonstationarity commonly arises in business metrics and can make A/B tests inefficient or invalid if not addressed.
The paper introduces a framework for appropriate modeling and statistical analysis of nonstationary A/B tests.
It proposes a continuous-time-covariate estimator, establishes a central limit theorem, and reports optimal asymptotic variance.
It proposes time-grouped randomization when possible and uses numerical experiments to illustrate the theory.

source_observation.claim: Time nonstationarity can undermine the efficiency or validity of online controlled experiments.

interpretation.claim: Experiment analysis should account for temporal structure rather than treating observations as stationary by default.

application.claim: For A/B tests with temporal variation, consider time-aware estimation or time-grouped assignment when the design phase allows it.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify when the proposed methods are unnecessary or how they perform under particular types or magnitudes of nonstationarity.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the assumptions of the framework, estimator, or limiting regime.
The abstract does not provide numerical experiment settings or quantitative results.
The abstract does not describe the scope of the optimality claim beyond asymptotic variance.
